findings.checklist_item: Derive `landed_text` through the SAME inbound decoder the Jira-side key uses (`InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` / `_normalize_comment_body`), not `codec.decode_inbound`, so both dedup keys are produced by one decoder (bug 17c3 invariant).
evidence: outbound_comments.py:538 builds the Jira-side key via `_normalize_comment_body(raw, inbound_mapper=inbound_mapper)`
outbound_comments.py:205 `_normalize_comment_body` calls `_resolve_inbound_mapper(...).normalize_rich_text(body)`
rich_text.py:158-162 DC `decode_inbound` is identity on str (returns body unchanged)
Plan Context cites bug 17c3 / 8209097fa9 'one decoder': 'BOTH keys must be produced by ONE decoder' (outbound_comments.py:575)
findings.finding: The plan's landed_text formula uses codec.decode_inbound, but the Jira-side dedup key decodes via InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text; on the DC codec decode_inbound is identity-on-str while normalize_rich_text normalizes wiki markup, so the two sides decode differently and the key can never match — reopening the two-decoder drift that bug 17c3 (8209097fa9) closed.
scenarios: A DC (jira_datacenter) comment whose wire form differs from its plain text under normalize_rich_text: local landed_text (codec.decode_inbound = identity) != Jira key (normalize_rich_text), so it re-posts every pass
findings.suggested_fix: Specify `landed_text = _normalize_comment_body(codec.to_wire(wire_body), inbound_mapper=inbound_mapper)` (or equivalently strip_marker(inbound_mapper.normalize_rich_text(codec.to_wire(wire_body)))) so the local key uses the identical decode path as the Jira-side key at outbound_comments.py:538.
